findings.comment: Clear, standalone first sentence. Begins with 'Returns', no @return needed. Correct wiki-link, appropriate altitude.
Same pattern as toByte; consistent and correct.
Same pattern as toByte; consistent and correct.
'Returns this value unchanged.' is concise, accurate, and matches the pattern in Int.scala and friends.
Precision caveat folded into the description as a trailing clause - clean, no @return needed.
Same pattern as toFloat; consistent and correct.

The description 'Returns `x` converted to a [[scala.Float]].' begins with 'Returns' but omits the precision caveat, which is instead pushed into the @return. The @return is therefore justified (it adds the missing edge case), but the split is mildly inconsistent with the sibling `toFloat` doc, which folds the caveat into the description and drops @return entirely. Consider: 'Returns `x` converted to a [[scala.Float]], which may lose precision.' and drop the @return. Minor: @return uses backtick `Float` while description uses wiki-link `[[scala.Float]]`; prefer the wiki-link form consistently.

Same nit as long2float: precision caveat lives only in the @return, inconsistent with the toDouble sibling. Consider folding into the description and dropping @return. Also, @return uses backtick `Double` while description uses `[[scala.Double]]`.
